title: Clinical Appraisal of Darkly Pigmented Fundus Lesions
summary: A comprehensive diagnostic framework for evaluating pigmented fundus lesions, ranging from benign choroidal nevi to sight-threatening uveal melanoma and choroidal metastasis. Precise differentiation requires a synthesis of clinical examination, multimodal imaging, and rigorous monitoring protocols.

content.explanation: To Find Small Ocular Melanoma Using Helpful Hints: Thickness > 2mm, Fluid (subretinal), Symptoms (blurred vision/flashes), Orange pigment (lipofuscin), Margin (near optic disc), Acoustic Hollowness (on B-scan), Halo absence.

sections.title: Red Flags: When to Biopsy or Refer
content: Thickness > 2mm measured on EDI-OCT or B-scan
Presence of symptoms related to the lesion site

sections.title: Pathophysiology & Histology
sections.content: Pigmented fundus lesions arise from melanocytes (nevi, melanoma) or RPE cells (CHRPE). Uveal melanoma originates from uveal melanocytes and often undergoes GNAQ/GNA11 mutations. Pathologically, it exhibits spindle cells (A/B) or epithelioid cells, the latter carrying a higher metastatic potential. Invasion through Bruch's membrane results in the classic 'collar-button' configuration.

sections.title: Diagnostic Workup Protocol
content: Step 1: Clinical Slit-lamp Biomicroscopy with Indirect Ophthalmoscopy (90D/20D lens).
Step 2: Fundus Autofluorescence (FAF) to detect lipofuscin (hyper-autofluorescence).
Step 3: Enhanced Depth Imaging OCT (EDI-OCT) to measure lesion thickness and detect SRF.
Step 4: Ultrasonography (A/B-scan) for internal reflectivity and thickness measurement.
Step 5: Fluorescein Angiography (FFA) to evaluate vascularity and 'double circulation'.
Step 6: Systemic evaluation (Liver function tests, abdominal ultrasound/CT/MRI) if malignancy is suspected.

sections.title: Key Clinical Pearls
content: Most choroidal nevi are dormant; do not biopsy unless suspicious.
Always document lesion location in relation to the optic disc in disc diameters (DD).
A halo around a nevus is a benign feature indicating stable/regressing margins.
B-scan ultrasonography is gold standard for measuring thickness of elevated lesions.
Genetic testing (BAP1, SF3B1, EIF1AX) is crucial for prognostication in melanoma.
